summary: Request: privacy-preserving SIEM sample for forensic handoff with temporal scrubbing and resume-token manifest
description:
Issue summary: Customer requests a forensic-grade SIEM sample package for an ongoing audit. They require that exported events be temporally scrubbed (time-shift within a deterministic window), identifiers pseudonymized with HMAC keyed per-tenant, and an accompanying resume-token manifest so ingestion can be replayed by their SOC without raw PII.

Impact: Customer cannot complete regulator evidence submission until sample bundle is delivered in accepted format. This is blocking their audit sign-off and legal review.

Request details: deliver a compact NDJSON sample (<= 500k events) covering 24 hours of tenant activity, with:
- deterministic temporal scrubbing (shift timestamps by tenant-seed + manifest mapping)
- per-field reversible pseudonymization whitelist (user_id, session_id) using tenant HMAC (customer provided key material)
- keep original event ordering and provide resume-token checkpoints every 15 minutes
- manifest (signed) describing transformations, time-shift seed, algorithm versions, and KMS key IDs used
- delivery via pre-signed S3 link with object-lock for 7 days

Expected behavior: Redwood provides an evidence bundle that the customer's SOC can ingest into their Splunk/QRadar proof-of-playback harness with documented checksums and replay tokens.

Observed behavior: Customer reports previous export (SUP-701999) included raw user identifiers and lacked resume tokens; they flagged it during internal audit. This ticket requests an alternate delivery method that meets the regulator's evidence checklist.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer run a standard SIEM export job for tenant finsecure-prod for window 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z - 2026-02-01T23:59:59Z.
2) Request delivery using the 'compact-evidence' export profile.
3) Observe that downloaded file contains original user_id and timestamps and lacks resume-token manifest.
4) Customer submits to SOC and gets an error in ingestion indicating missing resume_token header.

Note: we reproduced locally in staging using the export tool and confirmed missing resume-token metadata in the manifest for the 'compact-evidence' profile prior to applying privacy transforms.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 10:05 - Triage by Support (Aisha): validated customer audit checklist and confirmed required fields.
2026-03-10 11:30 - Eng (Daniel): reproduced in staging; found export path skipped pseudonymization when 'compact-evidence' profile used without explicit --privacy flag.
Hypothesis: legacy compact profile predates resume-token and privacy pipeline changes; exporter falls back to legacy manifest schema so signature and token fields are not emitted.

Ran local debug: set ENV EXPORT_PRIVACY=1 -> manifest includes resume_tokens and pseudonymization metadata. Behavior suggests configuration gating in server side feature flag 'export.legacy_compact_enabled'.

Checked related dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/siem-exports/export-errors?var-tenant=finsecure-prod shows a spike on 2026-02-01 where manifest-signature-mismatch and missing-resume-token events increase.
Customer provided an HSM-wrapped key identifier and confirmed they can accept HMAC-based pseudonyms using tenant HMAC-KID 'projects/finsecure/keys/hmac-01'.
comments: Aisha Khan (Support) 2026-03-10: Thanks for the details. We'll prioritize a privacy-preserving delivery. Can you confirm whether FinSecure will provide a tenant HMAC key or require Redwood KMS to issue a wrapping key?

Rajiv Patel (FinSecure SOC) 2026-03-10: FinSecure will provide an HMAC key wrapped with their KMS; we will upload the wrapped key to the S3 staging area. Need manifest to list KMS key id and HMAC-algo SHA256-HMAC.

Daniel Wu (Eng) 2026-03-11: Reproduced. The compact profile bypasses privacy transforms when legacy flag is set. Proposing two workarounds: (A) Run 'evidence-export --privacy' which applies deterministic temporal-scrub and HMAC pseudonymization; (B) patch exporter to include manifest fields for legacy profiles. Which do you prefer?

Rajiv Patel (FinSecure SOC) 2026-03-11: Option A is acceptable if you can guarantee deterministic time-shift seed and provide a signed manifest. Please proceed with Option A and deliver a pre-signed S3 link. Also require object-lock for 7 days and MD5+SHA256 checksums.
Daniel Wu (Eng) 2026-03-12: Preparing export run in prod with privacy flag. Will upload to s3://evidence-deliveries/finsecure/2026-02-01/ and share manifest. ETA 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC.
resolution:
In Progress - export job with privacy transforms queued. Planned remediation steps: (1) run one-time privacy export for requested window with --privacy and tenant-wrapped-HMAC provided by customer; (2) generate signed manifest (RS256) including time_shift_seed, pseudonymization: {algo: HMAC-SHA256, kid: projects/finsecure/keys/hmac-01}, resume_tokens every 15m; (3) object-lock S3 upload and provide pre-signed URL + checksums; (4) follow-up run to bake config change: remove legacy bypass or ensure compact profile requires explicit opt-in.

Follow-ups assigned: ENG-ops task to remove export.legacy_compact_enabled by 2026-03-25 (linked INT ticket), and create a console toggle for privacy exports. Customer to confirm receipt and verify ingestion by FinSecure SOC.
